reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its observable purpose is educational, solving GSSSB examination mathematics questions with worked equations on a classroom-style board. The related publication is presented as ordinary commerce connected to the study material, and subscription requests do not establish a payment requirement, data request, or financial-participation condition.

Order at the link below to book a publication book with all the paper knowledge. https://pages.razorpay.com/gsssb148

opening.argument: The description directly links a viewer action to a promised benefit: viewers are told to “Join our telegram group for free study Material,” with an external Telegram URL supplied for that purpose. That is a low-barrier acquisition flow: joining is the requested action and free study material is the promised return. The same description also directs viewers to order a publication book through a Razorpay link, showing that the video actively moves viewers from educational content toward external participation and commerce. The classroom presentation provides credibility, but it does not eliminate the explicit action-benefit solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the book “ordinary commerce” does not answer the separate free-material solicitation. The description does not merely mention study resources; it tells viewers to join an external Telegram group in exchange for free study material. Likewise, the presence of worked equations does not negate the explicit direction to order through a payment-linked page. The relevant issue is the action-benefit pairing, not whether the video also teaches mathematics.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited wording does not establish that joining is required to receive anything, nor does it promise money, digital assets, withdrawals, or an unusually valuable reward. “Free study Material” is a description of an educational resource, while the separate book link is plainly identified as an order for a publication. The mathematics instruction remains the observable central activity, and the links do not by themselves establish deceptive acquisition.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an external Telegram group advertised as providing free material, an external Razorpay page for ordering a publication, an Instagram account, WhatsApp contact information, and a subscription prompt. The description therefore creates multiple off-platform routes for viewers to engage, while the video repeatedly establishes credibility through examination solutions. Even without a deposit or guaranteed financial return, the combination supports a scam reading in which a low-effort viewer action is exchanged for access to promised material. The educational setting can make that solicitation less conspicuous, rather than making it irrelevant.

The description advertises Telegram, Instagram, WhatsApp, and a Razorpay order page, and the sampled ending visibly shows a subscription prompt. Those are not necessary to solve the equations. Their accumulation is relevant evidence that the video is also designed to move viewers into external channels and actions.

The sampled frames show examination questions and worked calculations, while the cited risk signals establish distribution and commerce but not deception or a qualifying reward scheme.

The instructional framing may be precisely what makes the external solicitation persuasive and lowers resistance to the requested actions.
